string.text: After updating ZHOPA, use MCM's Reset to defaults before changing options so the latest recommended defaults take effect.

Master runtime switch. Turning it off immediately cancels ZHOPA tasks, removes its generated service squads, clears its runtime and save data, and stops its callbacks and patches. Save the game after disabling before uninstalling the addon. Changes already made to the world cannot be reversed.
ZHOPA ALIFE 2 is disabled. New saves no longer contain ZHOPA state.
ZHOPA ALIFE 2 is disabled, but cleanup is incomplete. Keep the addon installed and retry after loading the game.
Allows ZHOPA to control stalker squad movement and assign stalker tasks such as rest, patrol, hunt, artefact search, and trade.
Allows ZHOPA to control mutant squad movement and assign mutant tasks such as roaming, hunting, patrol, and rest.
Shows ZHOPA squad state on map markers and enables extra diagnostic console messages for debugging simulation behavior.
Allows managed stalker squads to visit traders, take available squad quests, complete them, and receive virtual money rewards. Turning it off safely cancels active quest work.
Fill service jobs with existing NPCs

Assigns suitable NPCs from squads across the whole base, including its linked smart terrains, to vacant trader, technician, medic and cook/barman jobs. No new NPCs are spawned and emissions no longer trigger replenishment. Service NPCs spawned by the old filler are removed during migration. Offline vacancies are confirmed after the level loads. Disabling stops new recruitment while keeping assigned NPCs. Owner-faction NPCs across the whole base are considered first, then neutral or allied donors; NPC faction is preserved. Hostility toward the owner or existing service factions blocks recruitment.

After all trader, technician, medic and cook/barman roles across the base are filled, recruits arriving NPCs for vacant defensive posts. Each NPC permanently leaves its donor squad, stops roaming and does not consume BASE_CAMPING squad capacity. Native guards and occupied physical posts are respected. Disabling stops new assignments while retaining existing guards.
Minimum time between checks of the same smart terrain, in real seconds. The queue is processed in small batches; vacancies wait when no suitable squad is available.

Lets online NPCs use ZHOPA looting rules for corpses and loose items. Disabled by default: leave it off to use vanilla looting, the more predictable choice for large mod packs. Artefact task pickup is unaffected.
Allows squads that fight or loot outside the loaded level to gain loot value and loot cargo in the offline simulation.
Allows offline artefact tasks to use virtual artefacts generated from anomaly settings when no suitable real artefact exists. Real artefacts are still preferred.
Enables squad trade behavior: online sales to traders, offline barter accounting, automatic rest/base trading, and dedicated trade route tasks.
Sets what fraction of item value NPC squads receive when selling gear to traders. A lower value slows squad income without changing NPC purchases.
In story mode, converts non-immune stalker squads on active psi levels into zombified squads. Immune factions are controlled by config.
After the Brain Scorcher is disabled in story mode, sends selected eligible stalker squads toward northern levels instead of leaving them in place.
Percent of eligible stalker squads selected for the northern migration event. Higher values move more squads toward Zaton, Jupiter, and Pripyat.
Allows stalker squads to choose exploration targets and travel to valid smart terrains that are useful for roaming.
Allows stalker squads to move into suitable smart terrains that need occupants or local presence.
Allows stalker squads to settle at suitable bases. The settings below control whether their stay is timed or permanent.

Enabled by default. Limits garrison stays, including the result of occupy quests. After camping, a squad resumes its interrupted task if it is still valid. Disabling makes current and new stays permanent; enabling starts a fresh timer for permanent garrisons. This setting is shared by all factions and mutants.

Length of a timed stay after arrival: 0.25 to 72 in-game hours, default 6. Shared by ordinary camping and occupy. A new value applies to new stays and when switching from permanent mode; it does not reset the remaining time of an ongoing stay.
Allows stalker squads to patrol between several valid smart terrains instead of staying at one location.
Allows stalker squads to pause movement during the night and then resume their previous task when rest is finished.
Allows stalker squads to actively pursue hostile squads or direct hunt targets instead of only moving between smart terrains.
Allows stalker squads to travel to anomaly smart terrains and collect artefacts through the online or offline artefact logic.
Favors destinations whose danger better matches the squad's experience. Novices favor safer areas, while veterans are more willing to travel north.
Controls direct hunt and revenge targets that are far above a squad's strength. Soft keeps every valid target, Balanced sometimes avoids severe mismatches, and Strict always avoids them.

Considers allies and enemies. Roaming favors less populated levels, counting living stalkers and incoming squads; the allied safety bonus diminishes as a level fills. Uses the same rules online and offline.
Lets factions favor lore-appropriate work, such as Duty hunting mutants, ecologists seeking artefacts, and ISG exploring northward.
Relative chance for a stalker squad to pick exploration when several task types are available. Set to 0 to remove it from weighted selection.
Relative chance for a stalker squad to choose a smart terrain that needs population or local presence.
Relative chance for a stalker squad to pick a patrol route between smart terrains.
Relative chance for a stalker squad to hunt enemies when a valid target exists.
Relative chance for a stalker squad to choose an artefact task when a valid artefact target exists.
Base chance for a stalker squad to choose a dedicated trade route. The chance increases when the squad carries valuable items to sell.
Relative chance for a stalker squad to visit a compatible trader with available NPC squad quests. Set to 0 to remove quest trips from weighted task selection.
How many in-game hours a stalker squad spends in regular rest before it can select another task.
How many in-game hours a stalker squad keeps patrolling before it can roll a new task.
Minimum real-time seconds a stalker squad waits in fallback rest when no valid task can be assigned.
Maximum real-time seconds a stalker squad waits in fallback rest when no valid task can be assigned.
Keeps the squad's current, assigned, and scripted target fields aligned so smart terrain logic, debug HUD, and task logic agree on the destination.
Stops online smart terrain jobs from pulling NPCs away from the squad's active ZHOPA task when vanilla logic tries to reassign them.
Allows squads to remember recent attackers and create revenge tasks against the squad that attacked them.
Allows hostile squads to target the actor with revenge behavior when the actor caused the retaliation event.
Percent chance that a valid revenge event caused by the actor becomes an active revenge task.
Allows hunt tasks to resolve damage, loot, and outcome while both squads are offline and close enough to fight.
Real-time seconds between offline combat checks for active hunt tasks.
Distance in meters at which two offline squads are considered close enough for hunt combat to resolve.
Allows mutant squads to roam toward valid smart terrains when they are not hunting or patrolling.
Allows mutant squads to search for and pursue hostile stalker squads according to faction relations and available targets.
Allows mutant squads to patrol between valid smart terrains instead of remaining in rest.
Relative chance for a mutant squad to choose a hunt task when a valid enemy target exists.
Relative chance for a mutant squad to choose a patrol route between smart terrains.
Relative chance for a mutant squad to choose free roaming when it has no stronger reason to hunt or patrol.
How many in-game hours a mutant squad spends resting before it can select another task.
How many in-game hours a mutant squad keeps patrolling before it can roll a new task.
Adds activity dialogue to managed squad commanders and lets the actor travel with a moving squad to its current destination.
Charges the actor for travelling with a squad. The commander states the price before departure.
Final multiplier for squad travel cost. Base price is 1,000 RU per kilometre.

Replaces shared stalker task switches and weights with the settings below. Mutants and zombified squads keep their separate settings.
When disabled, the shared settings on the Stalker simulation tab work exactly as before. Faction defaults match the current shared defaults.
Allows this faction to accept available NPC squad quests.
Relative chance to choose an available squad quest.
Allows this faction to choose exploration targets.
Allows this faction to move into suitable smart terrains.
Relative chance to choose smart population.
Allows this faction to settle at empty allied bases.
Allows this faction to choose patrol routes.
Allows this faction to interrupt travel and rest at night.
Allows this faction to pursue valid hostile targets.
Allows this faction to seek and collect artefacts.
Relative chance to choose artefact search.
Allows this faction to trade and choose trade routes.
Base relative chance to choose trade routes.
Allows this faction to pursue attackers after a squad member is killed.
Allows this faction to choose the actor as a revenge target.
